HIG.v3_note: Supporting tier, 4.0% weight in the final 14-name v3 portfolio (12.0% in the earlier 10-name v1 cut). v4 would keep HIG but at reduced conviction/size vs. v3, not as a core position.
kill_criteria: Business Insurance underlying combined ratio >91% for two consecutive quarters (was 89.3% Q2'26, up from 88.0% Q2'25)
Adverse general-liability/commercial-auto/A&E reserve development >$150M in any single quarter
Hartford Funds/Wellington sale delayed, renegotiated, or terminated
Core-earnings ROE <15% for two consecutive quarters (vs. management-stated 20.3% TTM)
Net FY1 sell-side EPS revisions stay negative for two more months with no fundamental offset
key_adverse_facts: Q2'26 GAAP EPS $4.68 vs core EPS $3.42 - gap driven by a $251M one-off tax benefit and $318M discontinued-ops income tied to the Hartford Funds sale, not operating performance

Q1'26: Business Insurance prior-year reserve development was $30M net UNFAVORABLE (vs $51M favorable in Q1'25); both Q1'26 and Q2'26 releases cite increases in general liability and commercial auto reserves (social-inflation pattern)
$165M A&E reserve increase Q4'25 plus $70M more in Q1'26 for legacy sexual-molestation/abuse exposures (1970s-80s policies) - a recurring adverse category, not one-time

Sept 25 2026 8-K: commuted a legacy asbestos & environmental reinsurance treaty with Berkshire's National Indemnity (in place since Dec-2016) for $1.12bn cash and a $497M pretax gain expected in Q3'26 - cash-positive, but HIG now bears more legacy A&E tail risk directly, without that cover

17 of 19 sell-side FY1 EPS revisions in the last 30 days were cuts (vs 2 up), primarily because the Hartford Funds divestiture removes a profitable earnings stream from consensus models, plus commentary on softening P&C pricing (KBW, Wells Fargo, Mizuho estimate cuts)
Business Insurance underlying combined ratio drifting up: 88.0 (Q2'25) -> 89.2 (Q1'26) -> 89.3 (Q2'26)

HIG.confidence_in_thesis: medium - strong core franchise and quant score, but recent GAAP beats lean heavily on non-recurring items and the underwriting cycle (BI underlying CR, casualty reserves) is showing early softening; one more quarter (Oct 29 report, first full quarter after the National Indemnity commutation) would raise or lower confidence materially

CINF.v3_note: Not a v3 holding; v3's capped '<=2 insurers' CIO slots were filled by AIZ and HIG.
kill_criteria: Consolidated combined ratio stays above 100% (underwriting loss) for a second consecutive quarter
Current-accident-year ex-catastrophe combined ratio continues rising past ~90% (was 88.1% Q2'26, up from 85.1% Q2'25)
Commercial Lines combined ratio fails to normalize back under ~95% within two quarters (was 104.1% Q2'26)
A sustained broad-equity-market drawdown >20% that visibly impairs book value per share (40% of invested assets are equities)
Net FY1 consensus EPS revisions remain negative for two more months without stabilization
key_adverse_facts: Q2'26 consolidated combined ratio 100.8% - an underwriting LOSS quarter, driven by Commercial Lines at 104.1% (vs 92.9% Q2'25) and Ohio severe weather 'nearly four times' the 5-year Q2 average
Current-accident-year ex-catastrophe combined ratio also rose YoY in Q2'26 (85.1% -> 88.1%), meaning the deterioration is not fully explained by catastrophe severity alone

Q2'26 GAAP EPS $8.05 was 5.6x operating EPS $1.43, almost entirely a $1.03bn after-tax equity-portfolio gain masking the underwriting loss; GAAP EPS here is materially an equity-market read-through, not an underwriting signal - use operating income/EPS
Sell-side estimate revisions skew negative: FY1 6 down/1 up, FY0 8 down/0 up in last 30 days, consistent with the Q2'26 miss
Personal Lines had unfavorable prior-year reserve development of $20M in Q4'25 alone, and its FY2025 combined ratio deteriorated YoY (103.6% vs 97.5% FY2024)
Share buyback volume was not disclosed/quantified in 3 of the 4 releases reviewed (Q1'26, Q3'25, Q4'25) - a genuine disclosure gap
data_conflicts: b1 composite decile is 9 (0.875, a top-decile score) yet live_rank is 62 and live_top30=False - inconsistent with how HIG (decile 10, composite 0.886, rank 20) and MTB (decile 10, composite 0.930, rank 35) rank relative to their own composite scores. Cause not resolved from data available; flagged for the quant/lead agents rather than guessed at.
CINF.confidence_in_thesis: medium-low - valuation is genuinely the cheapest of the three names and the FY2025 underwriting trend was excellent, but the single most recent quarter available (Q2'26) is a real underwriting loss with rising ex-cat losses and negative estimate revisions, so the thesis hinges on whether Q3'26 (~Oct 26) shows Q2 was a weather-driven blip or the start of a trend

MTB.v3_note: Not a v3 holding; added to the v4 valuation universe once b1_live_scores identified it in the live top-40.

Net charge-offs exceed ~50bps in any quarter (vs ~37bps guided for FY2026, 23-31bps actually delivered in the last 4 quarters)
CET1 falls below the guided 10.0% floor (was 10.19% Q2'26, down from 11.54% Q3'24)
Once disclosed, CRE-office nonaccrual/criticized balances show material deterioration - currently not broken out in materials reviewed
Efficiency ratio deteriorates persistently above ~60% (expenses already guided to the high end of the FY2026 range)

Management's own FY2026 guidance (Sept 2026 deck) implies NIM compresses slightly into 2H26 (to 'mid-3.60s' from 3.70-3.71% now), NII tracking to the bottom of its $7.2-7.35bn range, and expenses tracking to the top of its $5.5-5.6bn range - a mildly unfavorable mix
Guided FY2026 net charge-offs (~37bps) sit above the 23-31bps actually delivered over the last four quarters - management's own base case expects credit-cost normalization upward
CET1 has fallen from 11.54% (Q3'24) to 10.19% (Q2'26), approaching the low end of the guided 10.0-10.5% band, via aggressive buybacks (8% of shares in the trailing 12 months)
Q4'24 and Q4'25 earnings-release data could not be fully retrieved this session (SEC EDGAR intermittent 503s) - two gaps in the 8-quarter table are disclosed rather than filled with invented numbers
A Section 5.02 (officer/director change) 8-K filed June 16 2026 was not investigated in detail given the time budget
data_conflicts: b1 composite is 0.930 (decile 10, the highest of the three names) yet live_rank is 35 and live_top30=False - the same rank/composite inconsistency noted for CINF; not resolved from data available.
MTB.confidence_in_thesis: medium-high - four consecutive quarters of NIM expansion, improving credit quality on an absolute basis, the only net-positive sell-side revision trend of the three names, and fair valuation; tempered by the CRE/office disclosure gap and management's own guidance implying some 2H26 margin/credit normalization

cross_cutting_notes: All three names' EPS/combined-ratio/NIM figures in this pass are sourced directly from primary 8-K Exhibit 99.1 press releases (not XBRL), consistent with the lead's instruction that a filer-side XBRL EPS scale error was found in HIG's data.
